John Locke, Two Treatises of Government.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-locke/two-treatises-of-government

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John Locke, the author, died 1704.

First publication of the text used: 1689 (SE colophon: 'Two Treatises of Government was published in 1689 by John Locke.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the text is in the US public domain. The text was first published in 1689, so the 95-year US term from the latest first publication ended by 1 January 1785.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. Every person named above died in 1704 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever that country is.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Two Treatises of Government was published in 1689 by John Locke.
- Wikidata Q9353 (John Locke), P570 = 1704-10-28 and 1704-10-28; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Locke
